lines.japanese: にこにこアルバイター千歳の、色んなひととお話しちゃうぞシリーズ！
lines.english: Smiling Part-Timer Chitose Presents: Conversations with All Kinds of People!

lines.japanese: 「ぬるっと行こう！」
lines.english: “Let's keep it slippery!”

lines.japanese: さてさて、今日も男性スタッフ最後のお勤め、クローズ作業に入っております。
lines.english: Now, then. Once again, we'd reached the last duty of the day for the male staff: closing.

lines.japanese: 出だしも肝心ですが、明日に繋げる一日の締め、これもまた同じくらい大切なことだと思うんですよね。
lines.english: A good beginning matters, but the way you close one day and carry it into tomorrow matters just as much. Don't you think?

lines.japanese: そして、労働を通した様々な自我とのコミュニケーション。これってお仕事をしている上で、面白い部分のひとつだと思いません？
lines.english: And all the different personalities you get to know through work—isn't that one of the fun parts of having a job?

lines.japanese: 「ポリッシャーがけ終わりました！」
lines.english: “I'm finished with the floor polisher!”

lines.japanese: 俺が大きな機械での雑巾がけを終えて所定の位置へ戻すと、別の場所できびきび動いてた先輩の長井さんがやってきました。
lines.english: After finishing with the big floor polisher, I returned the machine to its proper place. Nagai, one of the more experienced employees, came bustling over from another part of the restaurant.

lines.japanese: 長井さんは、えーそうですねー、一言で評すならお喋りさん……というか、語りたがりさんです。
lines.english: Nagai was, um, let's see... If I had to put it in one word, a chatterbox. Or maybe somebody who just loved to talk.

lines.japanese: ご自覚はないのかもしれませんが、とにかくよく語っておられます。黙って聞いていると、取り留めのないことを延々語りつづけます。
lines.english: He might not realize it, but the man certainly loved to talk. If you just listened quietly, he'd ramble on forever about nothing in particular.

lines.japanese: こういう方に対しては、こちらは聞き手に徹し、たまに促し程度の相槌を打つだけで良いので気が楽です。
lines.english: With this kind of person, I could devote myself entirely to listening and supply the occasional encouraging murmur. Easy work.

lines.japanese: 「千歳君は動きが早くて助かるね。これなら１５分には終わるかな」
lines.english: “You move quickly, Chitose. That's a real help. At this rate, we should finish by quarter past.”

lines.japanese: 「あざっす、工藤さんに叩きこまれました」
lines.english: “Thanks. Kudo drilled it into me.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、彼は早く帰りたがるひとだからね。早く帰りたくないひとなんて、そりゃいないだろうけどさ」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. He's always eager to get home. Not that anybody actively wants to stay, of course.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。長井さんも多忙そっすもんね」
lines.english: “Right. You seem pretty busy yourself, Nagai.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、自慢にもならないけど、友達は多い方なのかな。地元の連中と、サークルの仲間と、ゼミのメンバーと、あとカノジョの友達と、こないだコンパで知り合った女の子と──」
lines.english: “Ha ha. It's hardly anything to boast about, but I suppose I have a lot of friends. My old crowd from home, the people in my club, my seminar group, my girlfriend's friends, the girl I met at that group date the other day—”

lines.japanese: 「──そう、相手しなきゃいけないのがいっぱいいるからさ、さほど時間があるわけじゃないんだよね。でも、早く帰りたいってだけでおざなりに働くのもどうかなって俺は思うんだ」
lines.english: —yeah, I've got lots of people to deal with, so it's not like I have much time. Still, I don't think it's right to do a halfhearted job just because I want to get home early.

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。それは自分も分かる気がするっすね」
lines.english: “Right. I think I know what you mean.”

lines.japanese: 「でしょ？　うん、千歳君は分かってるな。そう、このバイトだって、ただ漠然と金をもらうだけじゃなくて、また違う側面から見れば、他に得るものは沢山あるはずなんだよ」
lines.english: “Exactly. Yes, Chitose, you understand. A part-time job isn't just a way to get paid. Look at it from another angle and there are all sorts of other things to gain.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。触れるもの全てが勉強っすね」
lines.english: “Right. Everything we encounter teaches us something.”

lines.japanese: 「たとえばこの清掃作業なんてのも、将来的には役に立たないかもしれないよ。だけどいまここで、将来役に立たない清掃作業をしている、この一瞬一瞬の事実こそが大切なんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “Take this cleaning, for instance. Perhaps it will never prove useful later in life. Yet what matters may be the fact of each instant we spend, here and now, performing cleaning that will never prove useful later in life.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。青春は一分一秒が輝いてるっすね」
lines.english: “Right. Every minute, every second of youth shines.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、そういうこと。大切なのは結果じゃなくて経過なの。何をしたかじゃなくて、何をしていたか。振りかえった道の輝きひとつひとつこそが、その後の人生の大きな糧になるんだよね」
lines.english: “Yes. Precisely. What matters isn't the result but the process. Not what we did, but what we were doing. Every glimmer on the road behind us feeds the life that comes after.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。長井さんの話は分かりやすいっすね」
lines.english: “Right. You make things very easy to understand, Nagai.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ千歳君、君は若いのによく生き方が見えてるひとだね。先人の話を受けいれる土壌ができてるよ。うん、でも悲しいけど、君みたいなタイプは少ない側の人間なんだよな」
lines.english: “Ah, Chitose. You're young, yet you already see how one ought to live. The soil within you is ready to receive the wisdom of those who came before. Sadly, people like you are in the minority.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、たまにこっち側のやつと出会えると嬉しくなるね。ぶっちゃけ世の中バカばっかだろ。俺たちみたいな分かってる側の人間は、どうしたって口数を抑えなきゃいけなくなるもんね」
lines.english: “That's why meeting somebody else on our side is such a pleasure. Frankly, the world is full of idiots. People like us—the ones who understand—inevitably have to watch how much we say.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。長井さんは言葉を選んでる感じっすね」
lines.english: “Right. I can tell you choose your words carefully.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いるからね、何でもかんでも思ったこと口から垂れながしちゃうやつ。俺は品性疑われるから、ひとの悪口とかあんまり言わないようにしてるけど、それしかネタのない人間って話が広がらないんだよね」
lines.english: “Yes. Some people let every thought in their heads dribble straight out of their mouths. Personally, I try not to speak ill of others; it makes one look vulgar. But when that's a person's only material, the conversation never goes anywhere.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。あ、じゃあ自分ゴミ捨て行ってきます」
lines.english: “Right. Well, I'll go take out the trash.”

lines.japanese: 労働を通して、様々な自我とのコミュニケーション。どうです？　これってお仕事をしている上で、面白い部分のひとつだと思いません？
lines.english: All the different personalities you get to know through work. What do you think? Isn't that one of the fun parts of having a job?

lines.japanese: その日は長井さんの予想よりやや伸びて、１０時２０分に作業が終わりました。
lines.english: That evening, we ran five minutes beyond Nagai's estimate and finished at ten twenty.

lines.japanese: 我ながら、上出来なんじゃないでしょうか。
lines.english: Not bad, if I do say so myself.

lines.japanese: 「お疲れ様でーす！」
lines.english: “Good work, everyone!”

lines.japanese: フレッシュマンらしい元気いっぱいな挨拶と共に扉を開けたものの、スタッフルームは無人でした。
lines.english: I flung open the door with all the vigor of a fresh new employee, only to find the staff room deserted.

lines.japanese: 「星屑ロンリネス！」
lines.english: “Stardust Loneliness!”

lines.japanese: 無人なのにとりあえず叫んでおきました。
lines.english: Nobody was there, but I shouted it anyway.

lines.japanese: しぃーん……。
lines.english: Deafening silence...

lines.japanese: しかしそのあとに訪れる無音で、余計に寂しさが際立ってしまいました。
lines.english: The absolute silence that followed only sharpened my loneliness.

lines.japanese: むなしい。さっさと着替えて帰ろう。俺は自分のロッカーから私服を掴みあげると、パーテーションで仕切られた奥の更衣用区画へ歩いていきました。
lines.english: How depressing. I should hurry up, change, and go home. I grabbed my street clothes from my locker and headed for the changing area behind the partition.

lines.japanese: 「ちぇーっ、今日も日和子さんと一緒に帰ろうと思ったのになー」
lines.english: “Aww. And here I was hoping I could walk home with Hiyoko again.”

lines.japanese: 「見栄張って普段から一緒に帰ってるみたいな言い方すんなよ」
lines.english: “Don't show off by making it sound like you two always go home together.”

lines.japanese: 「うわー、英里子さんアナタいつも、本当に見計らったかのようなタイミングで出てきますよね。マジで俺のこと見張ってんじゃないすか」
lines.english: “Wow, Eriko. You always appear with timing so perfect it feels planned. Are you actually watching me?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん……実は私、鷲介君のこと……」
lines.english: “Y-yes... The truth is, Shusuke, I...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、覗かないでくださいね」
lines.english: “Oh, please don't peek.”

lines.japanese: 俺は運命の告白をパーテーションのドアで断ちきりました。
lines.english: I severed destiny's confession with the partition door.

lines.japanese: そのあとにドアが大きな音を立てて揺れたのは、位置からしてヤクザキックでしょうか。
lines.english: A moment later, the door shook with a thunderous impact. Judging by where it landed, Eriko had given it a full pro-wrestling big boot.

lines.japanese: 着替えながら壁越しに聞いてみます。
lines.english: I questioned her through the wall as I changed.

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに英里子さんいつからいたんすか」
lines.english: “By the way, how long have you been in here?”

lines.japanese: 「いつもの痛いリアクションのあたり」
lines.english: “Since that painfully embarrassing outburst of yours.”

lines.japanese: 「自分のことを棚に上げて？」
lines.english: “That's rich coming from you.”

lines.japanese: さっきと同じ位置からガコンという音が二回聞こえました。
lines.english: Two more tremendous impacts sounded from the same spot.

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、俺を見かけた時点ですぐに声かけてくださいよ。なんでわざわざ機を待つんすか」
lines.english: “And really, why didn't you say something as soon as you saw me? Why wait for your moment?”

lines.japanese: 「や、とくに話すこともなかったし」
lines.english: “Didn't have anything in particular to say.”

lines.japanese: 「ひどい！　そんなもんなくたって適当でいいじゃないすか！」
lines.english: “That's horrible! You can make something up even if you've got nothing!”

lines.japanese: 「えー、じゃ千歳、なんか私に話すことある？」
lines.english: “Fine. Chitose, is there anything you want to talk to me about?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そっすねー、じゃあご趣味は」
lines.english: “Uh, yeah, sure. And what, pray tell, are your hobbies?”

lines.japanese: 「見合いかよ」
lines.english: “What is this, a matchmaking interview?”

lines.japanese: 「芸能人で誰に似てるって言われる？」
lines.english: “Which celebrity do people say you look like?”

lines.japanese: 「合コンかよ」
lines.english: “What is this, a group date?”

lines.japanese: 「あの、べつにボケてるわけじゃないんで、いちいち的確なツッコミ入れないでください」
lines.english: “I'm not doing a comedy routine, so stop snapping back with the perfect punch line every time.”

lines.japanese: 「そんじゃえーと、英里子さんはいままでどんなバイトやってきました？」
lines.english: “All right, then. What kind of jobs did you have before this one?”

lines.japanese: 「ここの前？　あー、単発の販売とか、ファーストフードとか」
lines.english: “Before here? Hmm. One-off retail jobs, fast food...”

lines.japanese: 「へー、接客業ばっかっすねえ。接客業のエキスパートじゃないすか」
lines.english: “Huh. Nothing but customer service. You're practically an expert.”

lines.japanese: 「だって一番楽じゃん。客相手に笑顔振りまいときゃいいんだからさ」
lines.english: “It's the easiest kind of work, isn't it? All you have to do is smile at the customers.”

lines.japanese: 「いやまあ……はは」
lines.english: “Well... Ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 世の中には、それを不得手としている人もいるんですよ英里子さん。
lines.english: There were people in this world who found that very thing difficult, Eriko.

lines.japanese: 「千歳はまだライターのバイトやってんの？　はん、生意気な、バッグに本なんか入ってるし」
lines.english: “You still doing that writing job, Chitose? Hmph. Look at you putting on airs, carrying books around in your bag.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ちょっとアナタ！　勝手にひとの鞄の中見るなんて、プライバシーの侵害もいいところですよ！」
lines.english: “Wait! You can't simply go through another person's bag! This is a gross invasion of privacy!”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、自分でさっき、バッグん中見ろって言ったんじゃん」
lines.english: “You told us to look in your bag yourself a minute ago.”

lines.japanese: そんなこと……ああ、言ったか。
lines.english: I would never... Ah. I had, hadn't I?

lines.japanese: 「ふうん、ホントに細川玉木の二作目だ……」
lines.english: “Huh. It really is Tamaki Hosokawa's second book...”

lines.japanese: 扉の向こうでぱらぱらと本をめくっている気配。
lines.english: Beyond the door came the flutter of pages.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、そうっすよ。俺の愛読書っすから。玉木・大好き・俺元気！」
lines.english: “Yeah, that's right. I'm a devoted reader. Tamaki! Love her! I'm feelin' great!”

lines.japanese: 「けっこー折り目とか付いてんのな。へぇー意外、しっかり読んでんだ」
lines.english: “It's got quite a few creases. Huh. I'm surprised—you really did read it properly.”

lines.japanese: 「意外ってなんすか、失礼な。読みますよそりゃ」
lines.english: “What do you mean, surprised? How rude. Of course I read it.”

lines.japanese: 「や、千歳に感想聞いても、答え濁す感じだったじゃん？　だからパラ見程度なのかと思ってた」
lines.english: “When I asked what you thought before, you kind of dodged the question, remember? I figured you'd only skimmed it.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、そりゃ失礼な……」
lines.english: “Ha ha. How rude...”

lines.japanese: ていうか、あのときは読んですらなかったんですけどね。失礼なのは俺なんすけどね。
lines.english: Though at the time, I hadn't read a single word. The rude one had been me.

lines.japanese: 「で、どうよ」
lines.english: “So? What do you think?”

lines.japanese: 「なにがですか？」
lines.english: “What do I think of what?”

lines.japanese: 「だからコレ『米寿』の感想よ」
lines.english: “Of *Eighty-Eight*, obviously.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そっすねえ……」
lines.english: “Oh. Right...”

lines.japanese: 感想か。ふむ。
lines.english: My opinion. Hmm.

lines.japanese: もしレビューを書くのなら、いまのうち構想をまとめておくのもいい機会かな。
lines.english: If I intended to write a review, this might be a good opportunity to organize my thoughts in advance.

lines.japanese: よし、じゃあ、ちょっと草案のつもりで語らせていただきましょう。
lines.english: All right. Let me talk it through as a rough draft.

lines.japanese: 「その本の面白さはですね、えー、遊歩道の散歩みたいな感じっすかね」
lines.english: The appeal of that book is, um... kind of like taking a stroll along a promenade.
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「どこかへ行くことが目的じゃなくて、歩くことそのものが目的みたいな」
lines.english: “Your destination isn't the point. The walking itself is.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そういう抽象的なのはいいや。本の感想だけ言って」
lines.english: “Yeah, spare me the abstract stuff. Just tell me what you thought of the book.”

lines.japanese: 「生きいそぐひとだなあ。もったいない、各駅停車の旅にも愉しみはあるっていうのに」
lines.english: “You certainly hurry through life. What a waste. Even a journey on a local train has pleasures of its own.”

lines.japanese: 「あるかあ？」
lines.english: “Does it?”

lines.japanese: 「ありますよ。淡々と進むからこその情景とか、滲みでてくる情緒みたいな」
lines.english: “Of course. Precisely because it moves quietly, you notice the passing scenery and the emotion that gradually seeps through.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、この本はそういう読み方をしろって言いたいわけ。ジョーケー？　ジョーチョ？　うぇ、たりい」
lines.english: “Oh, so that's how I'm supposed to read it. Scenery? Emotion? Ugh, sounds like work.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、とっつきにくいし、好みはありますよね。でも、そのうち漬物とか苦瓜みたいに、ある日ふとその味わいに気付くときが来るかもしんないすよ」
lines.english: “Admittedly, it isn't easy to get into, and tastes differ. But like pickles or bitter melon, one day you may suddenly discover the appeal of its flavor.”

lines.japanese: 「慣れてくるとポリポリ噛みしめたりしてね。そしたらまた深い味が染みでたりしてね。おっ？　とか思って、つい二度三度と手が伸びちゃったりしてね」
lines.english: “Acquire the taste and you find yourself crunching thoughtfully away. Then some deeper flavor seeps out. You think, 'Oh?' and before you know it, your hand is reaching for a second and third helping.”

lines.japanese: 「へぇーえ。おまえ誉めるの上手いじゃん。なんか私までもっかい読んでみるかって気になってきたよ」
lines.english: “Huh. You're good at praising things. You've almost made me want to read it again.”

lines.japanese: 「ぜひ」
lines.english: “Please do.”

lines.japanese: 「読まないけどな」
lines.english: “I'm not going to, though.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで！」
lines.english: “Why not!?”

lines.japanese: 「千歳の言い分は成程と思ったよ。でも違うんだな、私があの本で『えー』って思ったのはそーゆーこっちゃなくて、それ以前の問題」
lines.english: “I get what you're saying, Chitose. But that's not it. That's not what made me go, ‘Ehh?’ about that book. My problem's more basic than that.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どういう問題ですか」
lines.english: “Wh-what problem is that?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあたとえば、主人公のジイさんどう思った？　なんか違和感なかった？」
lines.english: “Take the old man who's the protagonist. What did you think of him? Didn't anything feel off?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……まあ……違和感というか……」
lines.english: “Ah... Well... It wasn't so much that something felt off...”

lines.japanese: 「そーすね……その時点での、年老いた現状ばかりが強調されちゃって、そこまでに積み重ねられてきたはずの……なんていうか、経験とか年輪みたいなものが伝わってこないかな、ぐらいは思った、かも……？」
lines.english: Well... maybe it focuses so much on him being old now that you don't really feel all the... I don't know, experience or years he should've built up getting there. I did kind of think that, maybe...

lines.japanese: 「だろ？　だから読み方とか味わい方とか以前にさ、そういう人間描写みたいなとこが駄目なんだよ」
lines.english: “Right? So before we even reach ways of reading or savoring the book, the characterization itself doesn't work.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、駄目かどうかは読んだひとの主観次第でしょうけど」
lines.english: “Whether it works is ultimately up to the individual reader.”

lines.japanese: 「でも少なくとも、私と千歳で駄目に二票入ったじゃん」
lines.english: “But that makes two votes against it: yours and mine.”

lines.japanese: 「観察力が足りてないんだよ。や、そんな大層なもんじゃねーな。要は作者の見えてる世界が狭いんだろ。乾いた青春丸見えなんだよ、遊びたりてないのバレバレ」
lines.english: “She hasn't observed enough. Nah, it isn't even anything that grand. The author's world is narrow, that's all. You can see her whole dry adolescence on the page. It's obvious she hasn't had enough fun.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなもんこれからっすよ。細川玉木まだ若いんすもん、これからバリバリ青春してバリバリ視野が広がるんすよ」
lines.english: That's all still ahead of her. Tamaki Hosokawa's still young. She's got plenty of youth left to live and plenty of horizons left to broaden.

lines.japanese: 「だろ？　だったら背伸びしてねーで、いまは得意の乙女ラブコメ書いてりゃいいんだよ。あっちが面白くて人気あんのは確かなんだし」
lines.english: “Exactly. So she should stop reaching beyond herself and write the romantic comedies she's good at. Those are entertaining and popular. Nobody can deny that.”

lines.japanese: 「ええーっと、まあ、それは俺も多少……思いましたけど……」
lines.english: “Well... yes. I did think... something along those lines...”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: え！　えっ？　うそん、いまの声って……えええ！？
lines.english: What!? Wait. That voice just now... No. No way!?

lines.japanese: <8>\「ぎゃあああああーっ！」
lines.english: <8> “Gyaaaaaaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: <8>\　聞ーかーれーてーたー！
lines.english: <8> She heeeard uuuus!

lines.japanese: 俺の『米寿』を開きながらロッカーに寄りかかる英里子さん。そのかたわらに、やや俯き加減な日和子さんがぴしりと背筋を伸ばして立っておられました。
lines.english: Eriko leaned against the lockers with my copy of *Eighty-Eight* open in her hands. Beside her stood Hiyoko, head slightly bowed, spine perfectly straight.

lines.japanese: 思わず逃げそうになるものの、いいやもう逃げない、逃げると癖になるって紀奈子さんも言ってた、よし、思いとどまって咳払いひとつ。
lines.english: For an instant I nearly fled. No. I would not run anymore. Kinako had said running away could become a habit. Very well. I forced myself to stay and cleared my throat.

lines.japanese: 「え、えー、いまのはですね、その、メンフリ用レビューの草案でしてね、ほら、ああいうのってベタ誉め一辺倒だとヤラセっぽいじゃないですか。だもんで、ちょいと批判的な色を入れてですね……」
lines.english: U-um, what you just heard was, well, a rough draft of my review for Men's Freeze. You know, if it's nothing but nonstop praise it sounds fake, right? So I figured I'd mix in a little criticism...

lines.japanese: 「じゃあテキトーな批判なのかよ。そしたら結局ヤラセじゃん」
lines.english: “Then you didn't mean the criticism? That makes the whole thing staged anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、テキトーではないっすよ。実際に俺が思ったことなのは確かです」
lines.english: “No, no, I didn't make it up. Those were thoughts I actually had.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。そうですか」
lines.english: “I see. Very well.”

lines.japanese: 「アッ！　や、あのっ、それは──」
lines.english: “Ah! No, um, that was—”

lines.japanese: ──いや、まあ、いいか。嘘は言ってないし、どのみち原稿にはしようと思ってるんだ。
lines.english: —but perhaps it was fine. I hadn't lied, and I intended to put it in the article anyway.

lines.japanese: 「……はい。そうです。いまのがおおむね本音の感想です。実際読んでていくつか気になる点はありました」
lines.english: “...Yes. That was more or less my honest opinion. Several things did trouble me as I read.”

lines.japanese: 「でも最初に言ったとおり、総じて俺はこの作品が好きです」
lines.english: “But as I said at the beginning, taken as a whole, I like this book.”

lines.japanese: 言いながら英里子さんの手から『米寿』を取りあげました。
lines.english: As I spoke, I took *Eighty-Eight* from Eriko's hands.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんはふてくされたような硬い表情で答えました。それが照れ隠しなのか、俺への反発心なのか、よくは分かりませんでした。
lines.english: Hiyoko answered with a stiff, almost sullen expression. I couldn't tell whether she was hiding embarrassment or bristling at me.

lines.japanese: 「自分の作ったものと真剣に向かいあっていただけるのは、それだけでも有りがたいことです」
lines.english: “I'm grateful simply to have someone take my work seriously.”

lines.japanese: 「だから千歳さんの感想、素直に受け止めさせていただきます」
lines.english: “So I'll take your comments to heart.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうも」
lines.english: “Th-thank you.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さん、怒ってはいない……のかな。
lines.english: Hiyoko wasn't angry... was she?

lines.japanese: 微妙に喜んでるようにも見えるんだけど……さすがにそれはポジティブシンキングが過ぎるか。
lines.english: She almost seemed faintly pleased... but perhaps that was optimism taken too far.

lines.japanese: げっ、なんか口とがらせてブツブツ文句言ってる……聞こえないふりしとこ。実際聞こえなかったけど。
lines.english: Oh, hell. She was pursing her lips and muttering complaints... I'd pretend not to hear. Though in truth I couldn't hear her anyway.

lines.japanese: 「でー、千歳の感想をまとめると、結局つまんなかったってことでしょ」
lines.english: “So, to sum up Chitose's opinion, the book was boring.”

lines.japanese: 「えええ！　いったいアナタこの至近距離でなにを聞いてたんですか。このわずかな間には次元の歪みでも生じているんですか」
lines.english: “What!? What exactly were you listening to from right beside me? Is there some dimensional rift between us?”

lines.japanese: 「だっておまえの言い分って、要は読者にオモシロ探ししろってことじゃん。本当に面白いもんは、わざわざ探さなくたって分かるっつーの」
lines.english: Because what you're saying is basically that readers have to go looking for what's interesting. If something's really good, you can tell without having to hunt for it.

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからですね、そういう入ってくる系の受動的な面白さと、見出す系の能動的な面白さはまったく別モノでしてね」
lines.english: “No, you see, passive pleasure that comes to you and active pleasure that you discover are completely different things.”

lines.japanese: 「面白いに種類とか関係ねーだろ。面白いか面白くないか、ふたつにひとつじゃん」
lines.english: “Who cares what kind? It’s either entertaining or it isn’t. That’s it.”

lines.japanese: 「ああもう、じゃあホラたとえば──」
lines.english: “Oh, for heaven's sake. Then take this passage—”

lines.japanese: 俺は手の中の文庫本をばばばと素早い動作でめくりました。
lines.english: I riffled rapidly through the paperback in my hands.

lines.japanese: 「──ハイここ。『恋の完成形とはなにか。焦燥、懐疑、欺瞞。幾重にも摩擦と和解を重ねて心通いあった先に、到達点はあるのか。仮にそれを婚姻、交配とするならば、親の子への愛とはいかに尊いものだろう』」
lines.english: “—here. 'What is the final form of love? Impatience, suspicion, deception. Beyond the heart's countless frictions and reconciliations, beyond the moment when two souls finally commune, does any destination await? If that destination be marriage and procreation, how sacred, then, is a parent's love for a child?'”

lines.japanese: 「ホラここ。いいでしょ。面白いとか面白くないじゃなくて、ね、なんかいいでしょ。うーんって、なんとも言えない感じになるでしょ」
lines.english: “There. That's good, isn't it? It isn't entertaining exactly. It's just... good. It leaves you thinking, with a feeling you can't quite put into words.”

lines.japanese: 「そう……ですか、ありがとうございます。そこは親戚の愚痴に基づいて私なりの言葉にしました」
lines.english: “I... see. Thank you. That passage was based on a relative's complaints, which I rendered in my own words.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、やっぱな、実体験じゃないんだ」
lines.english: “Ah. Thought so. It didn't come from experience.”

lines.japanese: 「幸せな恋愛したことないやつが言いそうだもん、いかにも。だいたい男も知らないやつが家庭を語るなんて、基礎とばして応用に挑むようなもんじゃん。無理あんでしょ。たとえば──」
lines.english: “It sounds exactly like something a person who's never had a happy romance would say. And writing about family when you've never even been with a man is like skipping the basics and attempting the advanced course. Of course it won't work. Take this—”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは俺から『米寿』を奪いかえすや、ぺぺぺと左手でページを繰りました。
lines.english: Eriko snatched *Eighty-Eight* back from me and flipped briskly through the pages with her left hand.

lines.japanese: 「──こことか『孫が部屋に来るのは、なにかねだるものがあるときだけ。近頃は足音だけでも分かるようになってきた』。こんないじけたジイさんいねえよ。そんなん込みで嬉しいんだよ、あいつらは」
lines.english: “—right here. ‘My grandson comes to my room only when he wants something. Lately, I can tell from his footsteps alone.’ No old man sulks like that. That's part of what makes them happy.”

lines.japanese: 「そう……ですか、すみません。そこはみのさんへの投稿葉書に基づいて私なりの言葉にしたんですが……」
lines.english: “I... see. I'm sorry. I rewrote that passage from a postcard somebody sent to a television advice show...”

lines.japanese: 「どうでもいいすけど、英里子さんページめくるの早いすね。まるで分かってたみたいに」
lines.english: “This is beside the point, but you're awfully quick at finding those pages, Eriko. Almost as though you knew exactly where they were.”

lines.japanese: 「なっ……なんだよ、そんなわけないだろ」
lines.english: “Wh... What? Don't be ridiculous.”

lines.japanese: 「いやー、でもなかなか楽しっすねえ、細川先生を囲む会」
lines.english: “This Tamaki Hosokawa roundtable is pretty fun.”

lines.japanese: 「囲んでねーよ。あーもー、ワケわかんない。いい、もう帰る」
lines.english: “This isn't a roundtable. Ugh, none of this makes any sense. Fine. I'm going home.”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは『米寿』を俺に突きかえすと、そのまま戸口へ向かいました。
lines.english: Eriko thrust *Eighty-Eight* back at me and headed for the door.

lines.japanese: 「あ、お疲れさまっすー」
lines.english: Oh, good work today.

lines.japanese: 「お疲れさまです」
lines.english: “Good night.”

lines.japanese: 「うーす。また明日なー」
lines.english: “Yeah. See you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: ちょっと照れくさそうな、でも後腐れのない元気な声が返ってきました。
lines.english: Her answer rang bright and free of resentment, though touched by a little embarrassment.

lines.japanese: ぱたんと閉じる事務室のドア。
lines.english: The office door swung shut with a soft click.

lines.japanese: あ。
lines.english: Ah.

lines.japanese: いま二人きりだ。
lines.english: We were alone.

lines.japanese: よっしゃ、ただいま何連敗中か忘れちゃったけど、今日も今日とて懲りずに帰りぎわ恒例の！
lines.english: Excellent. I'd lost count of how many times she'd turned me down, but it was time for tonight's traditional end-of-shift invitation.

lines.japanese: 「日和子さん！　それじゃあ我々も帰りましょうか！」
lines.english: “Hiyoko! Shall we, too, make our way home?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 「デスヨネー！　ハイそれじゃあお疲れさまですサヨウナラ～！」
lines.english: “Right, figures! Well, good night and fareweeeell!”
“Wait... What...?”

lines.japanese: もしかして……いま俺、拒絶されなかった……？
lines.english: Had she... not rejected me just now...?

lines.japanese: うそおおおおお！？
lines.english: No waaaaaay!?

lines.japanese: 絶叫が漏れそうになるのを慌てて抑えました。
lines.english: I hastily smothered the scream that threatened to escape.

lines.japanese: 「え、っと……じゃあ、あの、駅まで一緒に……帰り、ます？」
lines.english: “Um... Then, ah... shall we walk... to the station together?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。べつに、どちらでも」
lines.english: “I suppose. Either way is fine.”

lines.japanese: うぞおおおおォォォーん！！
lines.english: No waaaaaaaaaaaaaay!!

lines.japanese: あわ、わわ、あわわわわ……あまりの予期せぬ事態に、思わずガタガタ震えて恐慌状態に陥る俺。
lines.english: Ah-wha, wha-wha-wha... The utterly unexpected turn sent me into a trembling panic.

lines.japanese: いや、待て待て。落ちつけ、落ちつくんだシュウちゃん。ここでいつものように道化根性丸出しで「きゃっほうい、とうとう日和子さんと帰れル～ン！」とか叫んではまた逃げられてしまう。
lines.english: No, wait. Calm down, Shu. Stay calm. If I slipped into my usual clowning and cried, 'Yahoo! At last I get to walk home with Hiyokoooo!' she'd run away again.

lines.japanese: ふふふ、俺だって伊達に日和子さんを見てきたわけじゃない。あんたが千歳鷲介のような浮付いた男をお好みじゃないことぐらい、とっくにお見通しだぜ！
lines.english: Heh heh. I hadn't spent all this time around Hiyoko for nothing. I knew perfectly well that she didn't care for frivolous men like Shusuke Chitose!

lines.japanese: 言ってて悲しくなってきたけど、よしとりあえず今夜はハイテンション禁止、きゃっほうい禁止、帰れル～ン禁止、夜空にジャンプ禁止のナシナシ縛りで自重していこう。
lines.english: The admission was making me sad, but very well. Tonight's rules: no getting overexcited, no yahoo, no 'we're walking home togetherrr,' no leaping into the night sky. Restraint in all things.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそろそろ帰るぜ」
lines.english: “Well, time to head home.”

lines.japanese: クールに攻めても睨まれた！
lines.english: The cool approach earned me a glare too!

lines.japanese: 「米寿っていうのは８８歳のことらしいっすね」
lines.english: “Apparently *Eighty-Eight* is the traditional name for an eighty-eighth birthday.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、はい」
lines.english: “Yes. That’s right.”

lines.japanese: 「日本人女性って平均寿命が世界一高いらしいっすよ。八十何歳とかってニュースで言ってました」
lines.english: “I hear Japanese women have the world's highest life expectancy. Something over eighty, according to the news.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー、詳しいんですね」
lines.english: Wow, you know a lot.

lines.japanese: 「や、たまたまなんすけどね」
lines.english: Nah, I just happened to come across it.

lines.japanese: そして知ったのはたまたまでも、日和子さんとの話の種になると思って意識的に覚えといたんですけどね。
lines.english: And while the discovery had been chance, I had deliberately remembered it as potential conversation material for Hiyoko.

lines.japanese: いやあ、しかし、さっきは気が動転してしまい、我ながらどうなることかと思いましたが──
lines.english: Still, I'd been so flustered earlier that I'd wondered how this could possibly go—

lines.japanese: ──いざ並んで歩きだしてみたら、なんと話題の一発目が玉泉トレーナーの軽いお説教だったもので、まさに怪我の功名、いつもの調子を取りもどすことができました。
lines.english: —but once we began walking side by side, our very first subject was a mild lecture from Coach Tamaizumi. A blessing born of misfortune: it restored me instantly to my usual self.

lines.japanese: 好きな子に叱られて緊張がほぐれる俺ってどうなの？　という疑問についてはまた機会があれば。
lines.english: We can save the troubling question of why getting scolded by the girl I liked relaxed me for another day.

lines.japanese: 「日和子さんも、８８歳になってから自分の作品を読むと、また違った感じ方があんじゃないすかね」
lines.english: “When you read your own book at eighty-eight, Hiyoko, you may feel something entirely different.”

lines.japanese: 「う……若気の至りになりそうですね」
lines.english: “Ugh... It may look like a youthful indiscretion by then.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、いいじゃないすか若気の至り。至りましょう、尽くしましょう。ね、若いうちになんでもやっておきましょう」
lines.english: “Ha ha! Youthful indiscretions sound fine to me. Let's be young. Let's be indiscreet. Let's wring every drop out of it.”

lines.japanese: 「楽しいことも珍しいこともやって、色んなもの見て、色んなひとと話して、節操なく何でもかんでも吸収しとかないと、いざってときに後悔しちゃうかもしれませんよ、ハハー！」
lines.english: “Have fun, do strange things, see all manner of sights, speak with all manner of people. If we don't absorb everything we can, we may regret it when it matters. Ha ha!”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんって、ずいぶん悟ったようなこと言うんですね」
lines.english: “You talk as though you've got life all figured out, Mr. Chitose.”

lines.japanese: ええ、悟ってましたから。一時期は。
lines.english: Indeed. I had. For a while.

lines.japanese: ……悟ってたようなもんです。
lines.english: ...Or close enough.

lines.japanese: 「だったら、千歳さんも書いてみればいいんじゃないですか？」
lines.english: “In that case, why don't you try writing something yourself?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　何をすか？」
lines.english: “What? Writing what?”

lines.japanese: 「小説……とか」
lines.english: “A novel... perhaps.”

lines.japanese: 「えええ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ジャンル違いですけど、文章を書くことに関してアドバンテージは持ってるじゃないですか」
lines.english: “It's a different genre, but you already have a head start when it comes to writing prose.”

lines.japanese: 「好みは別れるところですけど、普段の言動にもユニークなセンスが見られますし」
lines.english: “Your sensibility won't be to everyone's taste, but even your ordinary words and actions are unmistakably your own.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、好み別れるんだ……」
lines.english: “Ah. Not to everyone's taste...”

lines.japanese: 「誉めてますよ」
lines.english: “I am praising you.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんはこちらをチラリとも見ずに、だけど何のてらいもなく言いました。
lines.english: Hiyoko did not so much as glance my way, yet spoke without the slightest self-consciousness.

lines.japanese: 「そーすか。いやあ、プロの作家さんからそんなお言葉をいただけると調子に乗っちゃいそーすねえ。ええ、じゃあ、機会があれば」
lines.english: Yeah? Man, hearing that from a professional writer might go to my head. Well, sure, if I get the chance.

lines.japanese: 「実際に書いてみたことはないんですか？」
lines.english: “Have you never actually tried?”

lines.japanese: 「はい？　や、だからおっしゃる通り、メンフリでちょこちょこ穴埋めみたいな記事書いてますよ？」
lines.english: Huh? No, like you said, I write little filler articles for Men's Freeze now and then.

lines.japanese: 「そういった活動も素晴らしいと思いますけど……」
lines.english: “I think that work is worthwhile too, but...”

lines.japanese: 「創作には興味ないんですか？」
lines.english: “Have you no interest in writing fiction?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、創作。創作は全然。いやあ、向いてないでしょ、飽きっぽいっつうか持続力ないんで」
lines.english: “Fiction? None at all. It wouldn't suit me. I get bored easily and never stick with anything.”

lines.japanese: 「勿体ない、素質ありそうなのに」
lines.english: “That's a shame. I think you have talent.”

lines.japanese: 「へっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんって、なんていうか、個性的なだけじゃなくて不思議な説得力があるんですよね」
lines.english: “There is something about you, Mr. Chitose. You're not just eccentric; there's a strange persuasive force to the way you talk.”

lines.japanese: 「もしそうした資質が、ある程度の文章力に支えられて一つの作品に結実したら……面白いもの出来ると思うんだけどなあ」
lines.english: “If those qualities were supported by solid prose and brought together in a single work... I think you might create something fascinating.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　それは買いかぶりすぎじゃないすかあ？」
lines.english: “Really? Aren't you giving me far too much credit?”

lines.japanese: 「私、ひとを買いかぶるタイプに見えます？」
lines.english: “Do I look like a person inclined to give others too much credit?”

lines.japanese: 「見え……ませんね」
lines.english: “You... do not.”

lines.japanese: たはー、困ったな。これって誉められてるんすよね。
lines.english: Whew. This was awkward. She really was praising me.

lines.japanese: 芸人殺しだな、日和子さん。普段いじられキャラで楽してるから、まともに褒めてもらっちゃうと、俺どう反応していいやら。
lines.english: Hiyoko had killed the bit stone dead. I was so used to playing the butt of the joke that when somebody praised me sincerely, I had no idea how to respond.

lines.japanese: こんなことなら日頃もっと褒められておくべきだったな。なんつって。
lines.english: I should have gotten more practice at being praised. Just kidding.

lines.japanese: 「興味あるジャンルとか、好きな作家とかはいないんですか？」
lines.english: “Are there any genres that interest you, or writers you admire?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、いまのマイブームは細川玉木っすかね」
lines.english: Well, right now I'm really into Tamaki Hosokawa.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ありがとうございます……」
lines.english: “Th-thank you...”

lines.japanese: あらら、いいかげん何度も言いつづけてるのに未だ照れちゃうあたり、日和子さんも褒められるのは得意じゃないのかしら。
lines.english: Goodness. Though I'd told her so repeatedly, the fact that she still grew embarrassed suggested Hiyoko was no better at receiving praise than I was.

lines.japanese: 「でも私程度じゃ参考にならないと思うんで、誰かもっとちゃんとした目標を見つけて、真面目に創作の道も考えてみたらいいと思います」
lines.english: “But I'm hardly a model worth following. Find somebody more accomplished to aspire to, and seriously consider writing fiction yourself.”

lines.japanese: うわ、照れ隠しなのか本気なのか、なんだか語気が強くなってきたような……困ったな。
lines.english: Oh dear. I couldn't tell whether she was hiding embarrassment or speaking in earnest, but her voice seemed to be gathering force...

lines.japanese: 「短編からでも一度書いてみたらどうですか？」
lines.english: “Why not try writing a short story, just once?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええじゃあ、機会があれば……」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. If the opportunity arises...”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ……機会があれば機会があればって、いったいあなたの機会はいつになったら訪れるんですか」
lines.english: “Honestly... 'If the opportunity arises,' 'if the opportunity arises.' When precisely do you imagine this opportunity of yours will arrive?”

lines.japanese: 「そっすねえ、それはまあ、機会があれば？」
lines.english: “Hmm. When the opportunity presents itself?”

lines.japanese: 歩きながらチラリと横をうかがえば──
lines.english: As we walked, I stole a sideways glance—
“Oh, honestly...”

lines.japanese: ──わ、目が合った。ていうか笑ってる。
lines.english: —whoa, our eyes met. Wait, she's smiling.

lines.japanese: ああくそう、かわいいなあ！（教官のときは怖いくせに！）
lines.english: Damn it all, she was adorable! (And so terrifying whenever she was training me!)

lines.japanese: 「あ、ちょっと待っててください。俺、切符買ってくるんで」
lines.english: “Wait here a moment. I'll buy my ticket.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは路線が違うから、本当なら俺は「じゃあここで」と言って別れるべきだったんでしょう。
lines.english: Because Hiyoko took a different line, this was where we should have parted.

lines.japanese: だけど一秒でも一緒の時間を延ばしたくて、俺はさりげなく彼女をそこに待機させてしまいました。
lines.english: But I wanted to stretch our time together by even one second, so I casually asked her to wait there.

lines.japanese: 券売機にはそれなりに列が出来ていましたが、それでも文句なく律儀に待っててくれる辺り、どうやら俺も以前ほどには嫌われてないみたいです。
lines.english: There was a decent line at the ticket machine. Yet she waited patiently without complaint, which suggested she no longer disliked me quite as much as before.

lines.japanese: 「すいません、お待たせしましたー」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you waiting.”

lines.japanese: 切符を買って日和子さんのもとへ戻りましたが、あれ、反応がない……駅のざわめきに負けて、俺の声が届かなかったのかな。
lines.english: I bought my ticket and returned to Hiyoko, but received no answer. Had the clamor of the station swallowed my voice?

lines.japanese: 「日和子さん？」
lines.english: “Hiyoko?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、はい！」
lines.english: “Ah! Yes!”

lines.japanese: やや俯いていた日和子さんに、斜め下から呼びかけてみました。
lines.english: Her head was slightly bowed, so I bent a little to catch her eye.

lines.japanese: 「お待たせっす。行きましょか？」
lines.english: “Sorry about that. Shall we go?”
“Ah, yes...”

lines.japanese: 首肯するものの、なぜか彼女の足は動きませんでした。
lines.english: She nodded, yet for some reason her feet did not move.

lines.japanese: なんだろう。はっ！　まさか「イヤッ、今夜は帰りたくない！」的な展開が？
lines.english: What could it be? Ah! Was this the part where she cried, 'No! I don't want to go home tonight!'?

lines.japanese: なんてアホな期待を匂わせるような雰囲気でもありません。彼女の表情はもっとこう、なにか言いたそうな、言えなそうな、言いにくそうな……。
lines.english: But the mood gave me no reason to entertain even that idiotic hope. Her face looked more as though she wanted to say something, couldn't say it, found it difficult to say...

lines.japanese: 「どしたんすか？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: とりあえず聞いてみました。
lines.english: So I asked.

lines.japanese: 「あの、以前ここで、千歳さんと話していた女性の方――」
lines.english: “That woman you spoke with here before, Mr. Chitose—”

lines.japanese: 「うぐっ！」
lines.english: “Ghk!”

lines.japanese: わ、忘れかけてたのに痛いところを……いや後半からどうなったのか覚えてないけど。
lines.english: She had found the one sore spot I'd almost managed to forget... Though I still didn't remember what happened in the latter half.

lines.japanese: 「え、ええ、あのひとは、メンフリの俺の担当さんなんすよ」
lines.english: “Y-yes. She's my editor on *Men's Freeze*.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、やっぱり編集さん。実は以前、祥玄社さんでお見かけしたような気がしたんで……」
lines.english: “Ah, I thought she might be an editor. I had the impression I'd seen her at Shogensha once before...”

lines.japanese: そこまで言うと、また口をつぐんでしまう日和子さん。
lines.english: Having said that much, Hiyoko fell silent again.

lines.japanese: なんでしょう。米田さん、ていうか祥玄社がなにか……？
lines.english: What was this about? Did Yoneda—or rather, Shogensha—have something to do with...?
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さん。祥玄社。言いにくそうな表情。
lines.english: Hiyoko. Shogensha. A face struggling to speak.

lines.japanese: 「もしかして持ち込みのこと……」
lines.english: “Is this about the manuscript you submitted...?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: おっと。
lines.english: Whoops.

lines.japanese: いかんいかん、危うく知らないはずの情報を口にするところでした。
lines.english: Careful, careful. I'd nearly mentioned information I wasn't supposed to possess.
“...Well.”

lines.japanese: 「よく分かりましたね。はい、実は私、三作目の原稿を祥玄社さんに持ちこんだんです」
lines.english: “You guessed quickly. Yes. The truth is, I submitted the manuscript for my third book to Shogensha.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんですか」
lines.english: “Is that so?”

lines.japanese: ごめんなさい、知ってます。
lines.english: Sorry. I already know.

lines.japanese: とは言えませんよねえ、内密に教えてくれた米田さんにも迷惑がかかるし。
lines.english: But I could hardly say so. Yoneda had told me in confidence, and revealing that would cause trouble for her too.

lines.japanese: 「二作目のあと、担当さんから声がかからなくなって……それで、初心に戻ろうと思って持ちこんだんです」
lines.english: “After my second book, my editor stopped contacting me... So I decided to go back to basics and submit the manuscript myself.”

lines.japanese: 「そういう行動力って大事だと思います」
lines.english: “I think that kind of initiative matters.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「それが千歳さんと初めてお会いした、あの日だったんですけど──」
lines.english: “It was the day you and I first met, actually—”

lines.japanese: うわあ、それも思いだして欲しくない過去の一つだあ。
lines.english: Oh, wonderful. Another memory I'd rather she forgot.

lines.japanese: 「だけどまだ、返事がこなくて……」
lines.english: “But I still haven't received an answer...”

lines.japanese: あれから十日ぐらい、ですか。こういう場合、それが長いのか短いのか俺には分かりません。
lines.english: It had been about ten days. I had no idea whether that was long or short in such matters.

lines.japanese: 分かってるのは、日和子さんの担当者が、たぶんこの先その原稿に目を通すことはないだろうってことと──
lines.english: What I did know was that Hiyoko's editor would probably never read the manuscript—

lines.japanese: ──いま日和子さんがとても不安な気持ちで待たされていること。
lines.english: —and that Hiyoko was waiting in terrible uncertainty.

lines.japanese: 俺はフッと前髪を吹きあげました。
lines.english: I puffed out a breath, lifting my bangs.

lines.japanese: 「そういえば、さっき更衣室で俺の言った感想──」
lines.english: “Speaking of which, what I said in the changing room—”
“Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「──聞いてたんすよね。アレ書評の草案なんすけど、どうでした？」
lines.english: “—you heard it, didn't you? That was a draft of my review. What did you think?”

lines.japanese: 「どう、とは？」
lines.english: “What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、見当外れのこと言ってなかったかな、とか」
lines.english: “Mmm. Whether I'd said anything completely misguided, for instance.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……いえ、問題ないと思いますけど」
lines.english: “Oh... No. I don't think there was any problem.”

lines.japanese: 「個人的なことを言えば、書いた側の狙いも汲みとっていただけてたし、指摘点もその通りで参考になったというか……ありがたいご意見でした」
lines.english: “Speaking personally, you understood what I was trying to do, and your criticisms were fair and useful... I was grateful to hear them.”

lines.japanese: 「へっへ、俺って結構いい目してると思いません？」
lines.english: “Heh heh. I've got a pretty good eye, don't you think?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ……そうかもしれませんね」
lines.english: “Well... perhaps you do.”

lines.japanese: 「ほら！　その千歳鷲介が、細川玉木には太鼓判を押してんすよ。三作目？　大丈夫でしょ！　自信持ってくださいって、ハハ！」
lines.english: “There! And Shusuke Chitose gives Tamaki Hosokawa his absolute seal of approval. Her third book? It'll be fine! Have some confidence. Ha ha!”

lines.japanese: 「もう俺、新作出さないなんて言ったら、編集部に八つ墓村の格好して殴りこみにいっちゃいますね」
lines.english: “If they refuse to publish the new one, I'll dress like the madman from *The Village of Eight Gravestones* and storm the editorial department.”

lines.japanese: 俺は空想上の猟銃を構えて、改札の向こうにズドンと撃ち放しました。
lines.english: I shouldered an imaginary hunting rifle and fired a thunderous shot beyond the ticket gates.

lines.japanese: 「あの」
lines.english: “Um.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 俺が心の猟銃に弾を込めようとしいていたら、目の前で日和子さんはごそごそと鞄を漁りはじめました。
lines.english: As I prepared to reload the rifle in my imagination, Hiyoko began rummaging through her bag.

lines.japanese: 「実はいま、その原稿のデータを持ってるんです」
lines.english: “The truth is, I have the manuscript data with me now.”

lines.japanese: 上目遣いで俺の表情を確認しながら、一枚のＣＤケースを取りだしました。
lines.english: Watching my expression from beneath her lashes, she produced a CD case.

lines.japanese: 「え、その、持ち込みした三作目っすか？」
lines.english: “Huh? Um, the third story you submitted?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ……一応」
lines.english: “Well... more or less.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は気のない返事をすると、両手で中途半端な位置まで差しだしてきました。
lines.english: With an offhand reply, she extended the case halfway toward me in both hands.

lines.japanese: 「あの、図々しいお願いですけど、もしお時間があれば……」
lines.english: “This is presumptuous, but if you have the time...”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、いんすか！　読ませてもらっちゃっていんすか！」
lines.english: “What? Really!? You'll let me read it!?”

lines.japanese: 「さ、騒がないでください！　そんな大したものじゃないですから！」
lines.english: “D-don't make a scene! It's not that big a deal!”

lines.japanese: 思わず大きな声を出してしまったら、日和子さんは人目を気にしてＣＤを引っこめてしまいました。
lines.english: My voice rose without warning. Conscious of the eyes around us, Hiyoko withdrew the CD.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうか……千歳さんってパソコンお持ちじゃないんですよね。すみません、じゃあまた今度、プリントしたものをお渡しします」
lines.english: “Oh, of course... You don't own a computer, do you? I'm sorry. I'll give you a printed copy another time.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いっすよ。いまから２４時間の出力センターでも行ってきますから」
lines.english: “That's all right. I'll go to a twenty-four-hour copy shop now.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ！　だだ、駄目ですよ！　だって、そんな、お店のひとに見られちゃうじゃないですか！」
lines.english: “What!? N-no, you can't! Somebody working there might see it!”

lines.japanese: 俺は日和子さんの手からＣＤを奪おうとしましたが、ぐっと握りしめていて寄越してくれません。
lines.english: I tried to pluck the CD from Hiyoko's hand, but she clutched it tight and refused to surrender it.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そっか。持ち込み済みの作品だから、もう守秘義務みたいなの発生してるんすね」
lines.english: “Oh, because it's already been submitted? You're under some kind of confidentiality obligation?”

lines.japanese: 「そういうわけじゃなくて恥ずかしいんです！」
lines.english: “That's not it! I'm embarrassed!”

lines.japanese: なんだそりゃ。
lines.english: What kind of reason was that?

lines.japanese: 「えー、漫画原稿とかビジュアル的な版下ならまだしも、細かい文字モノにいちいち目を通す暇な店員なんていませんよ。絶対見ないですって」
lines.english: “Come on. If it were comic pages or artwork, sure. But no clerk is going to stand there reading pages of tiny print. They absolutely won't read it.”

lines.japanese: 「絶対なんて言いきれる根拠はあるんですか。そんなこと店員さんが言ってたんですか。何時何分何秒に言ってたんですか」
lines.english: “On what grounds can you say 'absolutely'? Did an employee tell you that? At what hour, minute, and second did they say it?”

lines.japanese: うわあ、日和子さんってたまに幼稚園児みたいなこと言いだすよな……。
lines.english: Wow. Sometimes Hiyoko said stuff straight out of kindergarten...

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ絶対っていう証拠見せてください」
lines.english: “Then show me your proof that no one will.”

lines.japanese: 幼稚園児……。
lines.english: A kindergartner...

lines.japanese: 「えーと、じゃあですね、駅前のネットカフェで出力してきます。たしかあそこのプリンター、カウンターの真横にあるんで。印刷中は俺が目の前を陣取って、他の視線から守りぬいてみせます」
lines.english: “All right, then. I'll print it at the internet café by the station. If I remember correctly, the printer is right beside the counter. I'll plant myself in front of it while it prints and defend every page from prying eyes.”

lines.japanese: 「また今度持ってくるって言ってるのに……そんなにすぐ読みたいんですか？」
lines.english: “I said I'd bring it another time... Do you really want to read it that soon?”

lines.japanese: 「見たいっす！　超見たいっす！　今すぐ見ないと、寝不足で明日のバイトを休んでしまいそうです！」
lines.english: “I do! Desperately! If I don't read it tonight, I'll be up thinking about it and miss my shift tomorrow!”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんはしばらく考えたあと、こくりと小さく頷きました。
lines.english: Hiyoko considered for some time, then gave a tiny nod.

lines.japanese: 「分かりました。明日はお客さんも多そうだし、千歳さんに休まれては困ります」
lines.english: “Very well. We expect many customers tomorrow, and I can't have you calling out.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、じゃあ」
lines.english: “Yes. Then...”

lines.japanese: 俺は手のひらを突きだしましたが、日和子さんはその上にＣＤを載せることもなく、なぜか自分の鞄へ戻してしまいました。
lines.english: I held out my palm. Rather than place the CD in it, however, Hiyoko inexplicably returned the case to her bag.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ネットカフェまでお付き合いします。ブースでパソコンを操作する係と、プリンターの前に立っている係とが必要なはずですから」
lines.english: “I'm coming with you. We'll need one person to operate the computer in the booth and another to stand guard at the printer.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　いや、そんないいっすよ。国家機密じゃあるまいし、そこまで完璧を期さなくても」
lines.english: “What? No, you don't need to do that. This isn't a state secret. We don't have to make the operation perfectly secure.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ千歳さんひとりに任せて、万が一にも情報の流出がないと言いきれるんですか。本当ですか。命かけられますか」
lines.english: “Can you guarantee that leaving it to you alone carries no possibility whatsoever of a leak? Truly? Would you stake your life on it?”

lines.japanese: 幼稚園児……。
lines.english: A kindergartner...

lines.japanese: まあ、でも、日和子さんとの時間が延長されるわけだからそれでいいや。
lines.english: Still, this meant more time with Hiyoko, so it was fine by me.

lines.japanese: 実はアレキサンダーへ戻って店のパソコンを借りる、という代案が閃いてはいたのですが、あえて俺は口にしませんでした。
lines.english: In truth, an alternative had occurred to me: we could return to Alexander and borrow the restaurant's computer. I deliberately kept it to myself.

lines.japanese: というわけで、その後ふたりでちょろっとネカフェへ行ってきました。
lines.english: And so the two of us made a brief visit to an internet café.

lines.japanese: もう夜も遅かったので本当に用件だけを済ませる程度でしたが、今日はずいぶん幸運に恵まれていたので、これ以上の贅沢は申しません。
lines.english: It was already late, so we did little beyond our stated purpose. But I'd already been absurdly lucky today, and I couldn't ask for anything more.

lines.japanese: いいお土産ももらったし。
lines.english: Besides, I had a wonderful souvenir to take home.

lines.japanese: タイトルは『いつだってプリズム』。
lines.english: Its title was *Always a Prism*.

lines.japanese: あんまり夜更かしするわけにも行かないけど、いまから寝るまでに、半分ぐらいは読ませていただきましょうかね。
lines.english: I couldn't afford to stay up terribly late, but I could probably read half before bed.

lines.japanese: いただきます、と。
lines.english: Time to dig in.
